evaluation_heuristic: Evaluate the configured commit_history artifact against original_user_request. For commit coverage, treat git_log as the authoritative commit sequence for the lineage and cutoff represented by that log. First determine whether every commit represented by git_log that is in scope under the original request is represented exactly once in commit_history, in correct chronological order; report all missing, extra, duplicate, or misordered commits explicitly. Then evaluate every semantic SUCCESS/FAILURE judgment contained in commit_history. Do not sample. For each recorded commit judgment, determine whether the status and rationale are supported by available evidence and by the original request definition: SUCCESS means the initiating user goal was met such that the user was satisfied with that commit; FAILURE means the goal was not met and/or additional work was necessary to meet it. Do not infer user satisfaction merely from absence of an immediate corrective commit. When the initiating user prompt or subsequent user feedback is not present in the supplied inputs, mark the semantic judgment INDETERMINATE unless the supplied evidence independently establishes the requested success/failure condition. Distinguish a commit that is merely an intermediate implementation step from a commit that itself failed its own initiating user request. Additional later work is evidence of FAILURE only when that later work was necessary to satisfy the same initiating user goal. Also evaluate whether every per-commit field required by original_user_request is present and semantically supported: commit number, description, all affected files, how each file changed, why each change was made, date/time, wider movement/pattern/goal when applicable, and success/failure evaluation relative to the initiating prompt. Return an exhaustive result. Do not truncate, sample, or collapse individual semantic evaluations.

input_inventory.role_in_evaluation: Authoritative ground-truth commit sequence and lineage
Evaluation target artifact containing commit-by-commit records and semantic judgments
Specification defining scope, mandatory per-commit fields, and success/failure definitions

missing_commits.explanation: Commit 032d73557b8f82c75b14f98ced8678e05751e294 ('Add GeminiSupervisor full commit history audit') created ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/commit history/commit-history.md and is present in git_log within the lineage paths, but was omitted from the artifact's commit records.

coverage_evaluation.explanation: The artifact covers 235 of 236 in-scope commits. While all 235 included commits appear in exact chronological order without duplicates or extraneous commits, commit 032d73557b8f82c75b14f98ced8678e05751e294 is omitted.

contract_evaluation.requirement: Complete lineage commit coverage for GeminiSupervisor and predecessor folder
contract_evaluation.evidence: git_log contains 236 commits along the lineage paths up through 032d73557b8f82c75b14f98ced8678e05751e294, whereas commit-history.md records only 235 commits.
contract_evaluation.required_change: Include commit 032d73557b8f82c75b14f98ced8678e05751e294 in the audit record.

contract_evaluation.requirement: Per-commit field presence: commit number, description, date/time, author, wider movement/pattern/goal
contract_evaluation.evidence: All 235 entries contain headings with commit numbers and SHAs, as well as Date/time, Author, Description, and Wider movement / pattern / goal metadata fields.

contract_evaluation.requirement: Per-commit affected files inventory and change explanation
contract_evaluation.evidence: Each commit entry includes a structured Markdown table listing every repository file affected, change type (A/M/D/R/C/T), and an explanation of how the file changed including diff line stats.

contract_evaluation.requirement: Per-commit rationale ('why each change was made')
contract_evaluation.evidence: Every commit entry contains a dedicated 'Why this commit was made' section grounded in commit metadata and run records.

contract_evaluation.requirement: Success/failure semantic evaluations relative to initiating prompt and user satisfaction
contract_evaluation.evidence: The artifact systematically infers SUCCESS from the mere absence of immediate corrective follow-up when no user prompt or feedback is recovered, and classifies normal intermediate implementation steps as FAILURE. The evaluation heuristic explicitly prohibits inferring user satisfaction from the absence of an immediate corrective commit and requires marking judgments INDETERMINATE when user prompt or feedback is missing.
contract_evaluation.required_change: Update semantic evaluations to INDETERMINATE whenever the initiating prompt or feedback is missing or unverified, and avoid classifying intermediate implementation steps as failures unless they failed their own initiating request.

required_corrections.correction: Revise all semantic SUCCESS/FAILURE determinations where initiating prompts or user feedback are unrecovered to INDETERMINATE, rather than inferring SUCCESS from the lack of immediate corrective commits.
required_corrections.reason: The configured heuristic mandates that user satisfaction cannot be inferred merely from the absence of an immediate corrective commit, and that missing initiating prompts or feedback require an INDETERMINATE judgment unless independently established.

required_corrections.correction: Do not classify intermediate implementation steps or passing intermediate checkpoints within multi-step state machine runs as FAILURE.
required_corrections.reason: The heuristic explicitly instructs the evaluator to distinguish a commit that is merely an intermediate implementation step from one that itself failed its initiating user request.
